title: fix(plugin-calendar): a week or day resize of an overnight event keeps its other edge (objectui#11060)
body:
Fixes #11060
Clause-②: no

## What changes

In the week and day views, a resize now moves ONE edge of the event and keeps the other where the event truly has it. The top handle changes only the start; the bottom handle changes only the end. The kept edge is the event's own instant, handed to `onEventDrop` unchanged, instead of being rebuilt from the grabbed piece's clipped bound (midnight for an overnight event, or the 15-minute drawn height for a short one). The direction is triage's (comment 5887217189).

## Premise check, at objectui `origin/main` `873284657`

- The drag state's `resize-top` carried `anchorEndMin` and `resize-bottom` carried `anchorStartMin`: the grabbed piece's `endMin` / `startMin`, clipped to its day. Confirmed.
- The pointer-up branches rebuilt BOTH edges on the grabbed piece's day with `setHours(0, minutes)`. Confirmed.
- The piece model's `Entry` carries the true event (`entry.event`) beside the clipped bounds, and the move (objectui#11037, PR objectui#11057) reads the event's own instants with `timedEventInstants(entry.event)` at pointer-down. Confirmed; the resize now does the same.
- Each piece carries ONE handle, not two. The top handle is drawn only on the event's first piece (`entry.isStart`) and the bottom handle only on its last (`entry.isEnd`). So "each handle on each of its pieces" is two cases per view: the top handle on the first piece and the bottom handle on the second. A structural case in the new pin file holds that reading.

## Measured before and after

A 22:00 to 02:00 event (2026-01-12 to 2026-01-13, suite zone UTC), as `onEventDrop` received it:

| Gesture | Before (red on `873284657`) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Week or day, top handle of the first piece to 21:00 | 21:00 → **00:00** | 21:00 → 02:00 |
| Week or day, bottom handle of the second piece to 03:00 | **00:00** → 03:00 | 22:00 → 03:00 |
| Top handle pressed and released without moving | 22:00 → **00:00** | 22:00 → 02:00 (as it was) |
| Bottom handle pressed and released without moving | **00:00** → 02:00 | 22:00 → 02:00 (as it was) |
| 23:00 → 00:10, top handle dragged to the foot of the first day | 23:30 → **00:00** | 23:40 → 00:10 (held one slot before the end) |
| 23:50 → 01:00, bottom handle dragged to the head of the second day | **00:00** → 00:30 | 23:50 → 00:20 (held one slot after the start) |
| 10:00 → 10:05, top handle to 09:00 | 09:00 → **10:15** | 09:00 → 10:05 |
| Preview label, top handle of the first piece at 21:00 | 9:00 PM – 12:00 AM | 9:00 PM – 2:00 AM |
| Preview label, bottom handle of the second piece at 03:00 | 12:00 AM – 3:00 AM | 10:00 PM – 3:00 AM |

The first run of the new pin file against the unchanged source: `Tests 11 failed | 6 passed (17)`. The six that passed are the structural case and the five same-day controls (top to 09:00, bottom to 13:00, both one-slot floors, and an event with no end), which are unchanged by design.

## How

- `TimeGridResizeDrag` replaces the two resize members of the drag union. It carries `keptMs`, the event's own end for the top handle or its own start for the bottom, read with `timedEventInstants(entry.event)` at pointer-down.
- `resizedEvent(drag, day, slotMinutes)` is what the drop writes and what the preview draws. The dragged edge's arithmetic is unchanged: the pointer's row on the grabbed piece's day, snapped, through `atGridMinutes`. The kept edge is returned unchanged. The one-slot floor is measured against the kept edge's row on that day's column (`gridMinutesOn`: below 0 on the day before, past 1440 on the day after). For a same-day event that row is the old anchor, so the floor is the old floor exactly.
- The preview draws the part of the result on the grabbed day and is labelled with the whole event's times, as the move preview is since objectui#11037.
- The move path, the month grid and the arithmetic of objectui#11005's ruling B are untouched.

**One departure from the order's suggested route, declared:** the suggestion kept the one-slot floor "when both edges fall on the same day". Here the floor applies wherever the kept edge falls. Otherwise a 23:00 → 00:10 event's top handle could be dragged to 00:00, leaving a 10-minute event, and the README's "Refuses to drag past `end − slotMinutes`" would stop being true. That case is pinned.

## Zone rows: none, measured

The order asked for a Los Angeles row only if the resize path reads a date-only value. It does not. The resize path's inputs are the `CalendarViewEvent` `start` / `end` instants; a stored date-only value is read upstream by `toDisplayDate` in `ObjectCalendar`, which this change does not touch. The kept edge is now that instant handed back with no clock arithmetic, and the dragged edge's arithmetic is unchanged. The zone-pin driver's result is in the verification section below.

## README and docs

`packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` says the top edge "Adjusts only `startDateField`; end is preserved. Refuses to drag past `end − slotMinutes`", and the bottom edge the mirror of that. `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` says "Resize start" adjusts "only the start time" and "Refuses to cross the existing end". All of these are true after this change, so both are left as they are.

## Verification

Every command below ran at the branch head `21d579e96`, from the worktree root, through the shared verify lock where it is heavy.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-calendar/`: `Test Files 57 passed (57)`, `Tests 392 passed | 95 skipped (487)`. 57 is the package's tracked test-file count, the new pin file included. The 95 skipped are zone cases that run only under the driver.
- The new pin file alone, verbose: `Tests 17 passed (17)`.
- The zone-pin driver, `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts`: `Tests 27 passed (27)`. It was run although no zone row was added, because its calendar pins (objectui#11005 and objectui#11037) exercise `CalendarView.tsx`.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-calendar^...' run build` built the dependency closure `type-check` waits on (exit 0). Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar type-check` exited 0. `tsc --listFilesOnly` shows both of its programs include the changed files; the test program includes the new pin file.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the two changed source files exited 0, with 0 errors and 24 warnings. None of the warnings is on a line this diff touches. The narrowing is declared: the package's lint population is its `lint` script, `eslint .` in `packages/plugin-calendar`. The diff's lintable files in it are these two; eslint's JSON output counts 2 files. `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` and `check:unreferenced-sources` all exited 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three changed paths answers NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

- The fix also covers two cases the card did not name, with the same cause: a short event's top handle wrote the 15-minute drawn end, and a kept edge lost its seconds (the old anchor was whole minutes). The first is pinned; the second is not pinned separately.
- Not measured, and not filed (a read-only inference): on the night the clocks fall back, a dragged edge placed in the repeated hour goes through `setHours`, which picks one of the two instants. That arithmetic is unchanged here, and it was the same before this change.
